# Using The Repository Harness
<!-- Generated by repo-harness-builder; source: core/docs:3.0 -->
<!-- doc-role:overview -->

Use the three generated skills as a loop: recover context, keep durable documentation current, then leave a verified handoff.

## Daily Workflow
<!-- doc-role:daily-workflow -->
1. Start or resume with `repo-harness-session-start` and state the objective. It recovers relevant context from the newest valid local backup under `.repo-harness/memory-bk/` and Engram when available, and reconciles it with current repository evidence, reports a scoped outcome, and inspects local Git state read-only. A remote-check question applies only when synchronization is relevant and safe. `conversationLanguage`: `english` or `espanol` sets the agent's reply language, not the documentation language. `responseStructure`: `standard` or `adhd-friendly`; the latter puts the answer first, in small chunks, with one question at a time. `explanationStyle`: `standard` or `plain-language`; the latter uses simple wording, short sentences, and defined terms. `timeZone`: an IANA name such as `America/Costa_Rica` dates everything the harness writes; without it the host-local zone applies. The saved conversation language wins over persona, host, model, and tool defaults; only your explicit instruction changes it. To save preferences, explicitly ask: “Save Spanish as my conversation language in the repository preferences.” Or edit `.repo-harness/state/preferences/user-preferences.json` by hand. The agent never saves them on its own. Startup reads the file at the next session start. The [response contract](../../.repo-harness/rules/response-contract.md) owns precedence.
2. Use `repo-harness-documentation` when durable documentation or visible project state needs updating.
3. Pause or close with `repo-harness-session-stop`. It verifies evidence and required documentation, then writes one local backup under `.repo-harness/memory-bk/`, then Engram when available. Only requested Git work triggers path screening and exact work-unit proposals under repository policy; unchanged authorization is not requested again.

## Integrated Availability
<!-- doc-role:availability -->
Gentle AI and Engram are independent optional capabilities. Use each at its owned operation boundary; block only when the operation or repository policy requires it. Surface failures without claiming missing guarantees or withholding the repository handoff.

## Congruence And Ownership
<!-- doc-role:ownership -->
Run `python3 .repo-harness/check.py` (`python` on Windows) after canonical skills or runtime projections change. The checker is read-only and reports whether generated runtime copies still match their canonical skills. Root `.gitattributes` keeps every text file LF on every operating system with one repository-wide rule, `* text=auto eol=lf`, which also protects the checker, the manifest, canonical skills, and runtime projections. Without it a CRLF checkout reports drift the checker cannot resolve and unchanged files look modified across systems. Files already committed with CRLF need `git add --renormalize .` once. Engram carries temporary cross-session context; repository files remain authoritative. Promote verified durable facts through the documentation skill.

## Approval Boundaries
<!-- doc-role:approval-boundaries -->
The daily skills inspect read-only by default. Outcomes are `ready`, `paused`, `blocked`, `failed`, `completed`, or `degraded`, scoped so optional Git failure does not fail successful continuity. Documentation writes require explicit conversational approval. Explicit safe-sync consent covers bounded fetch plus fast-forward-only integration. Explicit combined commit-and-push consent covers exact staging, commit, checks, one fetch preflight, and one push to the identified upstream. Commit-only and push-only remain narrow, and material changes invalidate consent. Dirty or diverged repositories stay local for human resolution, and no Git action is required for continuity. A builder run carrying an authority context also prints digests you can review without reading anything private: `authorityContextSha256`, `targetBindingSha256`, `planSha256`, and `generationSha256` binding them together, with premise values and decision statements shown as explicit redaction markers and each evidence item as a repository-relative locator and a digest. Check those locators are the files you expect, then approve. If something was wrong the host must refresh the context with a new material revision and preview again, because a corrected answer with an identical plan keeps the same `planSha256` and gets a different `generationSha256`. Batch mode starts only when you name it with one bounded task: the agent then asks its remaining clarification questions as one numbered list. Its answers are never approvals, and it ends with the task or the session; the [batch interaction rule](../../.repo-harness/rules/batch-interaction.md) owns its limits.

## Removing The Harness Manually
<!-- doc-role:manual-removal -->
There is no automatic uninstaller. The help command explains this guide read-only; it never deletes files.
1. Inspect `.repo-harness/manifest.json` and the actual files to list the installed harness skills, commands, and runtime copies. The manifest is an inventory, not permission to delete; preserve modified or unknown content. Inspect any separately installed builder folder too. Do not remove entire `.claude/`, `.opencode/`, or `.pi/` directories.
2. Keep project documentation (README, CHANGELOG, and `docs/`) and useful continuity, preferences, and backups by default. Preserve what you need before removing harness storage.
3. In shared `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `.gitignore`, and `.gitattributes`, remove only confirmed harness references or rules that are no longer needed. Keep unrelated content, including ignore rules used by other tools. Review other retained documents for links to removed paths and update only those references.
4. Show the exact proposed file deletions and edits, then obtain explicit approval. Remove only the approved harness-specific files; remove `.repo-harness/` last, and only after checking its contents for information to keep. Never delete the repository or other tools' files.
5. Review the diff when Git is available and check for remaining harness entry points and broken links. Start a fresh agent session; an existing session can retain loaded instructions. Do not run the removed checker or reinstall the harness just to verify removal.
